articles.title: [Editorial] Improving men's health in a changing world
articles.abstract: Many men are failing to thrive. Shorter life expectancies for men than for woman first emerged in the 19th century and the gap has continued to widen (albeit with geographical variations). Men have a higher burden of illness: global disability-adjusted life-years are 16% greater among men than women. The primary drivers of these differences include non-communicable diseases (cardiovascular disease, cancer, and diabetes), external causes (suicide, road traffic injuries, falls, and interpersonal violence), communicable diseases (respiratory infections, tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS, and hepatitis), and substance use (alcohol-related and drug-related harms).

articles.title: [Obituary] Paul Veys
articles.abstract: Pioneer of paediatric stem cell transplantation and Director of the Bone Marrow Transplant Unit at Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children, UK. Born in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, on Aug 7, 1960, he died of metastatic cholangiocarcinoma on July 18, 2026, in Winchelsea, UK, aged 65 years.

articles.title: Diagnostic Delays Associated With a Screening Trial of a Multicancer Early Detection Test
articles.abstract: To the Editor The article by Mr Mann and colleagues reported that regional participation in a population-based cell-free DNA–based multicancer early detection (MCED) trial was associated with a modest increase in diagnostic delay for patients referred for suspected head and neck, lung, and upper gastrointestinal cancers. The authors concluded that this delay is unlikely to materially influence the interpretation of trial results.

articles.title: Diagnostic Delays Associated With a Screening Trial of a Multicancer Early Detection Test—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We appreciate Dr Froehner’s thoughtful comments on our article reporting differentially higher diagnostic delay rates in regions participating in a population-based cell-free DNA–based MCED trial. As Dr Froehner notes, many health conditions are associated with poverty, as in the case of the lung, head and neck, and upper gastrointestinal cancers that we focused on in our study. Long-standing disparities in who receives preventive care, screening tests, and diagnostic follow-up contribute to these inequities.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Fecal Immunochemical Testing
articles.abstract: To the Editor The recent cost-effectiveness study by Dr Lee and colleagues provided important evidence supporting integrated gastric and colorectal cancer prevention through Helicobacter pylori stool antigen (HPSA) and fecal immunochemical test (FIT) co-testing. Co-testing with HPSA and FIT may offer a promising and economically attractive strategy in populations with high incidence of both gastric and colorectal cancers. Beyond demonstrating the potential value of this approach, the Taiwanese experience may also provide valuable lessons for countries seeking to strengthen cancer prevention programs.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Fecal Immunochemical Testing—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank Dr Huynh and colleagues for their thoughtful comments on our economic evaluation of HPSA-FIT co-testing. Rather than modeling a program developed de novo, we evaluated the incremental value of integrating HPSA testing into an established colorectal cancer screening program. Accordingly, infrastructure development costs were not included in our analysis; however, this should not be interpreted as suggesting implementation requires only minimal investment. Health system readiness varies considerably across countries, but we regard such heterogeneity as support for a staged implementation strategy rather than a limitation: countries with established FIT programs can readily add HPSA testing to existing stool-based testing pathways, whereas those with less mature systems may need to strengthen registries, laboratory networks, referral pathways, and treatment capacity.

articles.title: [Editorial] Sweating the details in exercise oncology
articles.abstract: The benefit of exercise alongside cancer treatment and recovery has primarily rested on association. However, two randomised trials, CHALLENGE and STAMINA, now supply the causal evidence that exercise oncology lacked. The pressing question is now one of implementation. STAMINA has already led to free exercise programmes for men undergoing treatment for prostate cancer in the UK and the European Society for Medical Oncology has updated their guidelines as a result of the CHALLENGE study.

articles.title: [Comment] Iberdomide for minimal residual disease-negative myeloma—from underdog to the spotlight
articles.abstract: The introduction of thalidomide and its derivatives—lenalidomide, followed by pomalidomide—has improved the therapeutic arsenal for multiple myeloma for more than two decades. These immunomodulators bind to cereblon, a component of the CRL4-cereblon E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, which results in the targeted degradation of the transcription factors Ikaros and Aiolos.1,2 Iberdomide belongs to the next generation of drugs, known as cereblon E3 ligase modulators. Its chemical structure is extended by an additional benzyl moiety bearing a morpholine group—which increases the molecular volume and the contact surface with cereblon, thereby enhancing its affinity and degradation potency compared with conventional immunomodulators.

articles.title: [Comment] Time to say goodbye to full-field digital mammography in population-based screening?
articles.abstract: 51 (96%) of 53 countries in the WHO European Region have national breast cancer screening programmes. Globally, 63% of all nations have established breast cancer screening programmes.1 Most of the European screening programmes are organised nationally and are population-based, focusing on women older than 50 years.1 Full-field digital mammography is the gold standard screening modality used in these programmes because of its clinical efficiency and cost-effectiveness.2

articles.title: [Comment] Comprehensiveness of national cancer control plans
articles.abstract: Cancer poses a disproportionate disease burden across different country populations. Beyond large international differences in cancer incidence, cancer survival varies globally, even between countries within the same continent or among those with publicly funded health-care systems.1–3 Therefore, much research in recent years has rightly focused on how countries with a relatively poor record in cancer control could narrow the gap separating them from high-performing peers.

articles.title: [Comment] The unfulfilled promise of effective cancer medicines priced beyond reach
articles.abstract: Every year, pivotal clinical trials are reported, showing major advances in cancer treatment. At the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) 2026 conference, results from the RASolute302 trial for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer established daraxonrasib, a RAS(ON) inhibitor, as a watershed moment in oncology.1 Among previously treated patients, daraxonrasib improved median overall survival by 7 months compared with chemotherapy and improved quality of life. Given that pancreatic cancer is among the most lethal of all cancers, the target was hitherto considered undruggable, and that the disease is accompanied by considerable suffering, this treatment was appropriately celebrated as a landmark success of drug development.

articles.title: [Comment] Rare earth elements and the fragile promise of cancer theranostics
articles.abstract: Radionuclide theranostics is transforming oncology by enabling more personalised treatment based on tumour biology. The approach pairs tumour-specific vectors with diagnostic and therapeutic radionuclides. Theranostics enables clinicians to confirm tumour targeting via molecular imaging before delivering targeted radiation with the same vector. Over the past decade, this approach has transformed treatment for neuroendocrine tumours and prostate cancer and is now expanding into additional malignancies and earlier stages of disease.

articles.title: [Comment] Why childhood cancer medicines need market shaping led by the Global Platform: toward market transformation
articles.abstract: The majority of children diagnosed with cancer do not have access to essential medicines.1 To address this reality, the Global Platform for Access to Childhood Cancer Medicines (Global Platform) was launched in February, 2025, by WHO and St Jude Children's Research Hospital, in collaboration with UNICEF and the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO).2

articles.title: [Correspondence] From biomarker actionability to surveillance utility in SERENA-6
articles.abstract: Nicholas C Turner and colleagues1 report extended SERENA-6 results showing sustained benefit in progression-free survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0·45, 95% CI 0·34–0·59; nominal p<0·0001) and improved second progression-free survival (HR 0·63, 0·46–0·86; p=0·0037) after switching from an aromatase inhibitor to camizestrant when ESR1 mutations were detected in circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA).1 These findings support ESR1 mutation as an actionable biomarker. However, treatment efficacy in patients with detected ESR1 mutations does not, by itself, establish the population-level utility of serial surveillance, which depends on its intended use and net effects across all patients tested.

articles.title: [Correspondence] BCG-unresponsive non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer
articles.abstract: We read with great interest the BOND-003 Cohort C results reported by Mark D Tyson and colleagues,1 showing durable complete responses with intravesical cretostimogene grenadenorepvec in patients with high-risk, BCG-unresponsive, non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer with carcinoma in situ.

articles.title: [Correspondence] BCG-unresponsive non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer – Authors’ reply
articles.abstract: We thank Pietro Scilipoti and colleagues and Man Sun and colleagues for their interest in our Article on BOND-003 Cohort C.1

articles.title: [Corrections] Correction to Lancet Oncol 2025; 26: 898–910
articles.abstract: Kirby AM, Finneran L, Griffin CL, et al. Partial-breast radiotherapy after breast conservation surgery for women with early breast cancer (UK IMPORT LOW): 10-year outcomes from a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3, non-inferiority trial. Lancet Oncol 2025; 26: 898–910—In this Article, in table 1, the row of data for the reduced-dose group under the heading Any breast cancer event (intention-to-treat population) has been amended. In the third paragraph of the Results, sentence three should have read “63 (3%) participants developed contralateral breast primary cancers (24 [4%] in the whole-breast group, 20 [3%] in the reduced-dose group, and 19 [3%] in the partial-breast group), 53 (84%) of which were invasive...”, sentence four should have read “Non-breast second primary cancers were reported for 159 (8%) patients (62 [9%] in the whole-breast group, 57 [8%] in the reduced-dose group…”, sentence six should have read “Three breast angiosarcomas were reported...”, and sentence nine should have read “Breast cancer-related events of any kind were reported for 170 patients… with a 10-year breast cancer-free-interval in…91·8% (89·3–93·7) in the reduced-dose group…”.

articles.title: [News] 70th IAEA General Conference
articles.abstract: Malawi's National Cancer Centre, opened in July, 2025, with support from the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) Rays of Hope initiative, is intended to bring several cancer services together in one facility. The centre provides radiotherapy and brachytherapy, alongside surgery and chemotherapy, reducing the need for patients to seek different parts of their treatment elsewhere. The centre was among developments highlighted at the 70th IAEA General Conference, held at the Vienna International Centre on Sept 14–18, 2026, as countries discussed efforts to expand cancer diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: [News] India reaches 8 million milestone in HPV campaign
articles.abstract: Earlier this month, India surpassed 8 million doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, Gardasil-4, administered under a nationwide campaign launched earlier this year. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare described the milestone as an important step forward in their goal of reducing cervical cancer in a country that accounts for roughly a quarter of global deaths from the disease. Four states have already reached 100% coverage of their target populations. However, the national picture is uneven, and experts say sustaining momentum will require overcoming vaccine hesitancy, misinformation, and the logistical demands of reaching eligible girls across a vast and diverse country.

articles.title: [News] US EPA repeals emission limits
articles.abstract: On Sept, 14, 2026, the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) under the Trump administration announced a rollback of Biden-era rules limiting greenhouse gas emissions from the country's coal-burning and gas-fired power plants. The EPA also proposed scrapping all other greenhouse gas emissions rules for the power sector implemented by the Biden administration, arguing that the regulations exceeded the agency's authority under the Clean Air Act.

articles.title: [News] Could Brazil's tuberculosis network detect lung cancer earlier?
articles.abstract: A 6 month landscape assessment has explored whether Brazil could use its tuberculosis and primary health-care infrastructure to detect lung cancer earlier. The assessment covered three states (Rio de Janeiro, Pernambuco, and Amazonas) and was conducted by PATH and Global Health Strategies. The project was funded by the Bristol Myers Squibb Foundation.

articles.title: [News] New UK National Cancer Board
articles.abstract: The UK Government has formed a new National Cancer Board to drive delivery of its 2026 National Cancer Plan, a strategy blueprint aimed at transforming cancer care and outcomes in England by 2035.

articles.title: [News] Viet Nam considers health insurance for cancer screening
articles.abstract: Viet Nam's Ministry of Health wants to add screening and early diagnosis for seven cancers to services reimbursed by the Health Insurance Fund, potentially shifting a system that has largely financed cancer care after diagnosis towards earlier detection. But the draft decree would phase in coverage and leave the Ministry of Health to define target groups, services, and payment levels, with implementation tied to the fund's ability to pay.

articles.title: [News] 2026 ASTRO Annual Meeting
articles.abstract: Historically, prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) is associated with improved survival but increased neurological toxicity. Paul Brown (Mayo Clinic, Rochester, MN, USA) presented results from the phase 3 SWOG S1827 MAVERICK trial, comparing standard-of-care, PCI plus MRI, with MRI surveillance alone in 304 randomly assigned patients with limited and extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) who had completed initial therapy. The median follow-up was 22 months and the primary endpoint, cognitive failure-free survival, was significantly better in the MRI only group (HR 0·60, 90% CI 0·46–0·78; p=0·001).

articles.title: [News] Impact of the Trump Administration on the Affordable Care Act
articles.abstract: On Sept 22, 2026, the US Government cancelled more than 760 000 people's government-subsidised health insurance policies, contending they were fraudulently obtained on the Federal Health Insurance Marketplace. As many as 440 000 other enrolments are still under investigation, officials said.

articles.title: [News] Europe has fallen behind in number of oncology trials
articles.abstract: The proportion of the world's oncology trials delivered within Europe has fallen from 41% in 2008 to 21% in 2023, according to a new report by the European Cancer Organisation (ECO).

articles.title: [News] Russia slashes federal cancer funding to spend on defence
articles.abstract: Cancer experts fear a rise in cancer cases in Russia if a draft 2027 budget proposing a sharp cut of more than 90% in federal cancer funding is pushed through parliament.

articles.title: [Perspectives] Beyond words: the Art of Living
articles.abstract: Some places shape not only the careers we build, but the people we become. For me, that place is the Cape Breton Cancer Centre (Sydney, NS, Canada). In 2001, I began my career as a radiation therapist, never imagining that this cancer centre would become one of life's greatest teachers.

articles.title: [Perspectives] Alison Berner: Connecting oncology and gender medicine
articles.abstract: It was a 2015 Editorial in The Lancet Oncology discussing cancer in the transgender community, that set Alison Berner (Queen Mary University of London, London, UK) on her unique career path.1 The Editorial cited a piece of research in people with HIV, which she realised meant there was no relevant papers in transgender people with cancer to draw on.

articles.title: [Perspectives] There is beauty after breast cancer
articles.abstract: Joanne Tinker remembers searching online for what a mastectomy would look like, convinced she was about to be mutilated. She was not. The gap between fear and reality is what a new exhibition in Ilkley (UK) sets out to close.

articles.title: [Articles] Iberdomide plus daratumumab and dexamethasone versus daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (EXCALIBER-RRMM): an open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: Iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone significantly improved MRD-negative complete response compared with daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone. The most common grade 3 or grade 4 adverse events were haematological events and infections, which were mostly manageable with standard supportive care. These findings support iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone as an efficacious treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma with the potential to be administered across diverse care settings.

articles.title: [Articles] Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial
articles.abstract: TOSYMA-2 indicates that about a quarter of invasive interval cancers occurring with digital mammography over 2 years might be avoided with digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screening. Although the primary outcome of TOSYMA-2 did not reach statistical significance, this large, randomised trial adds substantial evidence to the use of digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography in breast cancer screening.

articles.title: [Articles] Assessment of comprehensiveness of national cancer control plans using a multiagent artificial intelligence model: a global analysis
articles.abstract: Our analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data.

articles.title: [Articles] Global uptake of essential cancer medicines with and without complex genomic diagnostics: a retrospective observational study
articles.abstract: These findings should be interpreted as evidence of associations not causality, suggesting differences in quantity uptake of essential cancer medicines along two structural dimensions: fewer countries showed uptake of essential cancer medicines in lower-GDP countries than in middle-GDP and high-GDP countries and medicines requiring complex genomic diagnostics had lower uptake, with the lowest uptake in lower-GDP countries. The results suggest that, as precision oncology medicines become increasingly represented in the WHO EML, EML inclusion alone could be insufficient to enable patient access.

articles.title: [Articles] Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted.

articles.title: [Articles] Global health expenditures on cancer control: a cross-sectional analysis
articles.abstract: Our findings indicate high variability of per-capita health expenditure on cancer control globally and generally low expenditure levels, particularly in lower-middle-income and low-income countries and territories. The paucity of publicly available expenditure data on cancer control indicates the need for production of detailed NHAs that include disease-specific expenditures to ensure availability of regular, comparable, and reliable data.

articles.title: Chronotherapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors: The knowns, the unknowns, and the contested
articles.abstract: Emerging data indicate that immune checkpoint inhibitors can exhibit time-of-day-dependent effects in pre-clinical models. Furthermore, multiple retrospective clinical trials associate earlier anti-tumor treatment timing with improved outcomes. However, key questions remain regarding the reproducibility of these findings, the underlying mechanisms, and their clinical implications. This commentary discusses these open questions and provides an outlook on the field.

articles.title: Human-centric preclinical models for CAR T cell therapy in solid tumors: Where patient-derived organoids fit
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has shown promising activity in solid tumors, yet translational progress remains limited by preclinical models that incompletely capture human tumor biology. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) preserve key features of human tumors, including cellular heterogeneity and tissue architecture, thereby enabling functional evaluation of CAR T cell targets, next-generation approaches, resistance mechanisms, and selected safety considerations. We discuss how PDOs complement existing preclinical platforms to support CAR T cell development for solid tumors.

articles.title: γδ T cells BiTE back at small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Ng et al. characterize and leverage cytotoxic γδ T cells in small cell lung cancer to overcome unsuccessful checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. Engaging Vδ2+ cells with a bispecific T cell engager (BiTE) bypasses the challenge of low MHC-I expression and ineffective CD8+ T cells.

articles.title: Microbial cues for a stem-like lymphoid niche
articles.abstract: While tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) broadly correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, their functional heterogeneity can translate into divergent clinical outcomes. In this issue of Cancer Cell, Hu et al. uncover a microbiota-orchestrated stem-like lymphoid niche in which CD70+ ILC2s sustain progenitor exhausted T cells, and their findings redefine the functional organization underlying TLS-associated antitumor immunity.

articles.title: Teamwork makes the dream work? Ensemble learning in computational pathology
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Luo et al. report an ensemble approach that integrates five pretrained pathology foundation models into a slide-level representation to exploit their complementary information, yielding improvements in tumor subtyping, biomarker, and therapy-response prediction. This shows the potential of ensemble and multimodal approaches in computational pathology.

articles.title: Hitting KRAS G12D without the gut punch: Can immunotherapy make it last?
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Shi et al. report encouraging early-phase results combining HRS-4642, an allele-specific KRAS G12D inhibitor, with the PD-L1 inhibitor adebrelimab in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer. The intravenous combination was safe and well tolerated, notably sparing patients the gastrointestinal toxicity common to oral KRAS inhibitors, and achieved a promising 43% response rate at the recommended dose.

articles.title: Beyond genes and hotspots: Protein-informed interpretation of cancer mutations
articles.abstract: Interpreting the biological and clinical significance of somatic mutations in cancer genomes remains challenging. In this issue of Cancer Cell, Hyeon et al. identify and map significantly mutated regions to protein domains and structural features, establishing a proteo-genomics framework for interpreting cancer mutations beyond genes and hotspots.

articles.title: The wu wei of brain metastases: When the gift of a pause is also a vulnerability
articles.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, García-Gómez et al. show that brain-seeding cancer cells exploit an MXD4-dependent proliferative pause that enables survival under stress before metastatic outgrowth. By restraining MYC and activating protective stress responses, this pause becomes an Achilles’ heel, potentially targetable to eradicate micrometastases before clinical relapse.

articles.title: Tumor cells recruit macrophage bodyguards to outlast chemotherapy
articles.abstract: In Cell Press Blue, Carvalho et al. identify spatially organized tumor-macrophage niches, EMT-like CD44high cancer cells paired with SPP1/PARP14high macrophages, that drive chemoresistance in bladder cancer. PARP14 inhibition can flip this protective niche into an inflammatory, cisplatin-sensitizing state.

articles.title: Beyond BMI: The diet-microbiome context of the obesity paradox
articles.abstract: In Nature, Desharnais et al. show that in diverse mouse models, anti-PD-1 sensitivity is more closely linked to diet-microbiome-metabolite ecosystem than to obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction. Their findings reinforce body mass index (BMI) as an incomplete proxy for host biology and suggest strategies to improve anti-PD-1 efficacy without inducing obesity.

articles.title: γδ T cells modulate anti-tumor immunity in small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: Ng et al. show that γδ T cells infiltrate SCLC and have cancer-fighting abilities. These cells can be harnessed through multiple therapeutics to kill SCLC, including through MHC-independent recognition mechanisms via BTN2A1. Notably, γδ T cell infiltration is clinically relevant in SCLC, with high levels predictive of improved outcomes with αPD-L1.

articles.title: Ensemble learning of pathology foundation models for precision oncology
articles.abstract: Luo et al. develop ELF, a framework that ensembles five pathology foundation models to generate unified representations from whole-slide images. Trained on nearly 54,000 slides across 20 anatomical sites, ELF outperforms individual foundation models in disease classification, biomarker detection, and prediction of response to chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy.

articles.title: UniCure: A multi-modal model for predicting personalized cancer therapy response
articles.abstract: Chen et al. present UniCure, a multi-modal foundation model that predicts drug-induced transcriptomic responses across diverse cellular contexts. By bridging cancer cell line data with patient-derived models, UniCure enables personalized drug prioritization and patient stratification, with its predicted therapeutic rankings correlating strongly with clinical survival outcomes in real-world cohorts.

articles.title: Myeloid reprogramming generates myeloid-derived activating cells to potentiate radiotherapy and suppress metastasis
articles.abstract: Ji et al. show that radiotherapy induces a TET2-dependent epitranscriptomic program in myeloid cells that promotes immunosuppressive M-MDSC differentiation. TET2 loss preserves caRNA m5C-MBD6 signaling, restores IRF3-IFN-I activation, generates myeloid-derived activating cells, and enhances radiotherapy-induced antitumor immunity.

articles.title: Intratumoral Bacillus cereus orchestrates stem-like lymphoid niches to potentiate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma
articles.abstract: Hu et al. integrate spatial multi-omics to identify stem-like lymphoid niches (SLNs) organized by CD70+ ILC2s and Tpex cells that predict PD-1/PD-L1 immunotherapy responses in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). They reveal that Bacillus cereus-PI-PLC increases SLN abundance and synergizes with PD-L1 blockade, highlighting microbiota-driven enhancement of cancer immunotherapy through SLNs therapeutically in HCC.

articles.title: Proteo-genomics-guided interpretation of somatic mutations in cancer genomes
articles.abstract: Hyeon et al. integrate protein structures with population-scale cancer genomics data to characterize significantly mutated regions in 173 cancer-relevant genes. These regions align with functional domains, three-dimensional structural constraints, and gene-specific biology, providing a framework for classifying mutation patterns in cancer genes and prioritizing sparsely annotated variants for clinical interpretation.

articles.title: A transient MXD4-dependent proliferative pause enables survival of brain micrometastases
articles.abstract: García-Gómez et al. identify a transient state, termed the proliferative pause, that enables the survival of micrometastases during vascular co-option by buffering organ-imposed stress. Targeting vulnerabilities associated with this state suppresses metastatic progression and relapse, revealing opportunities for preventive intervention.

articles.title: Chemotherapy enhances cancer vaccine efficacy and expands stem-like TCF1+CD8+ T cells
articles.abstract: Noblecourt et al. show that chemotherapy acts as an immunological adjuvant by expanding TCF1+CD8+ T cells during vaccine priming, thereby enhancing vaccine-induced anti-tumor immunity. These findings provide a rationale for combining chemotherapy, cancer vaccines, and PD-1 blockade in the clinic.

articles.title: Chemotherapy-free phase 1/2 trial of HRS-4642 plus adebrelimab in previously treated metastatic KRAS G12D-mutant pancreatic cancer
articles.abstract: Shi et al. report the first clinical study of the selective KRAS G12D inhibitor HRS-4642 combined with the anti-PD-L1 antibody adebrelimab in heavily pretreated patients with KRAS G12D-mutant pancreatic cancer. The chemotherapy-free regimen demonstrates a manageable safety profile and preliminary antitumor activity, supporting its feasibility as a targeted strategy in this molecularly defined subset.

articles.title: Retraction Notice to: Taxanes trigger cancer cell killing in vivo by inducing non-canonical T cell cytotoxicity
Oncostatin M and TGFβ1 divide the epithelial–mesenchymal landscape
articles.abstract:
Nature Cancer, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01271-7

Stabilization of the hybrid epithelial–mesenchymal state drives therapy resistance and metastasic progression. Dong et al. use integrated single-cell and spatial analyses to demonstrate that oncostatin M and TGFβ1, respectively, maintain hybrid and late epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition states within self-sustaining neutrophil- and macrophage-rich niches of squamous cell carcinoma.

articles.title: Myeloid-derived TGFβ1 and oncostatin M establish two distinct stromal niches controlling late and hybrid EMT states
articles.abstract:
Nature Cancer, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01259-3

Dong et al. conducted single-cell and spatial analyses in mouse skin tumors, revealing that myeloid-derived OSM and TGFβ1 establish distinct stromal niches that sustain hybrid and late EMT states, respectively.

articles.title: Targeting GALE harnesses γδ T cells for cancer immunotherapy
articles.abstract:
Nature Cancer, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01203-5

Cancer cells can evade the immune system through mechanisms such as downregulation of MHC I molecules and expression of inhibitory ligands. Research now shows that targeting the metabolic enzyme GALE in tumor cells boosts the killing of these cells by γδ T cells through altering the glycosylation of key immune-checkpoint ligands.

articles.title: GALE is a tumor-intrinsic checkpoint of Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated killing
articles.abstract:
Nature Cancer, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01249-5

Shan et al. identified UDP-galactose 4-epimerase as an immune checkpoint of Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated cancer cell killing by enhancing interaction of CD155 and CEACAM1 with their receptors TIGIT and TIM3, respectively, and simultaneously inhibiting CD155 binding to CD22.

articles.title: BAZ2A-induced epigenetic states in cancer cells fuel palmitate accumulation in the tumor microenvironment driving CAR-T cell exhaustion
articles.abstract:
Nature Cancer, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01267-3

Wang et al. reveal that epigenetic remodeling driven by BAZ2A in renal cancer cells induces the production of palmitate that is taken up by tumor-infiltrating cells, resulting in impaired metabolic fitness of CAR-T cells via PGC-1α palmitoylation.

articles.title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
articles.abstract:
Nature Cancer, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01265-5

Ogier et al. uncover that cancer-associated fibroblasts fuel pancreatic tumor growth and immune suppression by transferring membrane lipids to cancer cells through anoctamin 6-dependent trogocytosis.

articles.title: A genome‑wide screen in E. coli reveals metabolic adaptations that enhance intratumoral fitness and bacterial cancer therapy efficacy
articles.abstract:
Nature Cancer, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01263-7

Chen et al. conducted a genome-wide screen in E. coli to identify genetic determinants of intratumoral bacterial fitness and targets for therapeutic application.

articles.title: [Comment] Redefining curative treatment for early-stage mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer
articles.abstract: For decades, the standard of care for patients with resected stage II and III colon cancer has centred on surgery with consideration of postoperative adjuvant systemic therapy to reduce risk of recurrence. Mismatch repair deficiency is seen in 10–15% of non-metastatic colon cancers and is predictive of response to immune checkpoint inhibition. The initial report of the single-arm, phase 2 NICHE-2 study of one dose of ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) and two doses of nivolumab (3 mg per kg) before surgery with clinical stage II and III colon cancer generated considerable interest after demonstrating a remarkable 98% pathologic response rate, including a pathologic complete response rate of 68%.

articles.title: [Articles] Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial
articles.abstract: In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer.

articles.title: [Articles] Zamtocabtagene autoleucel, a tandem CD20–CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy, for second line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma in patients ineligible for transplantation (DALY 2-EU): primary analysis of an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 2 study
articles.abstract: The risk–benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.

articles.title: [Articles] Neoadjuvant niraparib monotherapy for unresectable, homologous recombination deficiency-positive, high-grade serous ovarian cancer (NANT): a multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial
articles.abstract: Neoadjuvant niraparib showed anti-tumour activity and enabled R0 resection in selected patients with HRD-positive advanced ovarian cancer who were initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery. This strategy remains investigational and requires randomised validation against standard platinum-taxane neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

articles.title: The cyclin-G associated kinase (GAK) is a clinically actionable drug target required for mitosis in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
articles.abstract:
Leukemia, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41375-026-03174-z

The cyclin-G associated kinase (GAK) is a clinically actionable drug target required for mitosis in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

articles.title: Clinical and molecular characteristics of FLT3-ITD microclones in elderly patients with acute myeloid leukemia receiving less-intensive therapy

articles.title: Iberdomide plus daratumumab and dexamethasone versus daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (EXCALIBER-RRMM): an open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Iberdomide, a cereblon E3 ligase modulator with enhanced antimyeloma and immunostimulatory activity compared with immunomodulatory drugs, has shown clinical activity in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma and synergy with anti-CD38 antibodies. EXCALIBER-RRMM, comparing iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone with daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone, uses minimal residual disease (MRD)-negative complete response and progression-free survival as dual primary endpoints. Here, we report the results of the primary analysis of MRD-negative complete response. METHODS: EXCALIBER-RRMM is an ongoing, two-stage, open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial done at 211 hospital and community-based sites in 31 countries. Eligible participants were adults (aged ≥18 years) with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, who had undergone one to two previous lines of therapy, had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance-status score of 0-2, achieved at least a partial response to previous treatment, and subsequently experienced disease progression. Patients with anti-CD38-refractory disease or bortezomib-refractory disease were excluded from both stages, whereas stage 2 permitted enrolment of up to 10% of patients with previous anti-CD38 exposure. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1 in stage 1 and 1:1 in stage 2) using interactive response technology to iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone or daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone. In stage 1, patients received iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone (oral iberdomide [1·0 mg, 1·3 mg, or 1·6 mg]; subcutaneous daratumumab [1800 mg]; and oral dexamethasone [40 mg or 20 mg for patients older than 75 years]) or daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone (subcutaneous daratumumab [1800 mg]; subcutaneous bortezomib [1·3 mg/m FINDINGS: 1163 patients were screened for eligibility of whom 939 patients were randomised, 279 in stage 1 and 660 in stage 2. 800 patients were randomised to the 1·0-mg dose of iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone or to daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone. The primary MRD analysis ITT population comprised the first 420 patients enrolled between July 14, 2022, and July 3, 2024: 207 in the iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone group and 213 in the daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone group. Of these 420 patients, 244 [58%] were male, 176 [42%] were female, median age was 68 years [IQR 60-73], and 257 [61%] were White. At a median follow-up of 15·7 months (IQR 12·8-23·2), MRD-negative complete response was achieved in 85 (41%) of 207 patients receiving iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone and 44 (21%) of 213 receiving daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone (stratified proportion difference 20·1% [95% CI 11·5-28·6, p<0·0001]; odds ratio 2·8 [95% CI 1·8-4·3]). Grade 3 or grade 4 adverse events occurred in 187 (92%) of 204 patients with iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone and 143 (70%) of 204 patients with daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone, including neutropenia (172 [84%] vs 23 [11%]) and infection (80 [39%] vs 44 [22%]). Serious adverse events occurred in 119 (58%) patients in the iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone group and in 83 (41%) patients in the daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone group; the most common was pneumonia (36 [18%] vs 13 [6%]). Three (1%) deaths (sepsis, listeria encephalitis, and unknown cause) in the iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone group and two (1%) deaths (one due to sepsis and pneumonia and one due to sepsis) in the daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone group were considered related to any study treatment by the investigator. INTERPRETATION: Iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone significantly improved MRD-negative complete response compared with daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone. The most common grade 3 or grade 4 adverse events were haematological events and infections, which were mostly manageable with standard supportive care. These findings support iberdomide, daratumumab, and dexamethasone as an efficacious treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma with the potential to be administered across diverse care settings. Assessment of progression-free survival, the second dual primary endpoint, is ongoing. FUNDING: Bristol Myers Squibb.

articles.title: On-demand transarterial chemoembolisation combined with atezolizumab and bevacizumab in patients with untreated hepatocellular carcinoma (TALENTACE): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: TACE is the standard treatment for intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma but has limited survival benefits. TALENTACE evaluated adding atezolizumab and bevacizumab to on-demand TACE versus on-demand TACE alone in patients with systemically untreated, intermediate-to-high tumour burden unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. METHODS: In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 study at 40 centres in China and Japan, patients aged 18 years or older with confirmed, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma and an anticipated life expectancy of 12 months or more were eligible for inclusion. Eligible patients were required to have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, Child-Pugh class A liver function, no previous systemic therapy, and a sum of tumour maximum diameter (cm) and lesion number of six or more based on the six-and-twelve score. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1), using a permuted-block method implemented via an interactive voice and web response system, to on-demand TACE plus atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously and bevacizumab 15 mg/kg intravenously once every 3 weeks (initiated 14 days to 8 weeks after TACE), or on-demand TACE alone, with TACE administered at the investigators' discretion. The randomisation sequence was generated by an independent biostatistician at the system vendor and was concealed from the sponsor study team and investigators until randomisation; allocation was stratified by baseline α-fetoprotein, prior locoregional therapy, and baseline Vp1/2 (and geographic region in earlier protocol versions). Primary endpoints were investigator-assessed TACE progression-free survival (TACE-PFS; time from randomisation to untreatable [unTACEable] progression, TACE failure or refractoriness, or death), and overall survival, both analysed in the intention-to-treat population. Overall survival was assessed under a prespecified adaptive (group sequential) design comprising two interim analyses and one final analysis. Safety was evaluated in the as-treated population, defined as all randomised patients who received any study treatment, analysed according to the treatment received. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04712643) and is ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Feb 23, 2021, and August 11, 2023, 342 patients were randomly assigned to TACE plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab (n=171) or on-demand TACE alone (n=171). Median age was 61·0 years (range 21·0-90·0), 66 (19%) of 342 participants were female, 276 (81%) were male, 308 (90%) were Chinese, and 34 (10%) were Japanese. The mean size of the largest target lesion per RECIST 1.1 was 7·7 cm (SD 4·3) in both arms. In the TACE plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab group, 36 (21%) of 171 patients were Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage A, 100 (58%) were stage B, and 35 (20%) were stage C; in the TACE alone group, 42 (25%) of 171 patients were Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage A, 105 (61%) were stage B, and 24 (14%) were stage C. At data cutoff (Feb 28, 2025; median follow-up 26·25 months [IQR 21·16-33·74]), median TACE-PFS was 11·30 months (95% CI 7·52-15·01) with TACE plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab versus 7·03 months (95% CI 5·32-8·41) with TACE alone (hazard ratio [HR] 0·71 [95% CI 0·55-0·92]; two-sided stratified log-rank p=0·0089). Overall survival remains immature and was assessed at the first of the prespecified interim analyses; median overall survival was 34·53 months (99·62% CI 24·80-not evaluable) in the TACE plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab group compared with 35·38 months (99·62% CI 24·74-not evaluable) in the TACE alone group (HR 0·96 [99·62% CI 0·58-1·58]). The most common grade 3-4 adverse events in the TACE plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab group were decreased platelet count (23 [14%] of 166), hypertension (23 [14%]), and post-embolisation syndrome (21 [13%]); in the TACE alone group, the most common were post-embolisation syndrome (23 [13%] of 173), decreased platelet count (12 [7%]), and increased aspartate aminotransferase (12 [7%]). The most common serious adverse event was ascites (eight [5%]) in the TACE plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab group and post-embolisation syndrome (six [3%]) in the TACE alone group. Treatment-related deaths occurred in five patients in the TACE plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab group (gastrointestinal haemorrhage, liver abscess, haemolytic anaemia, hypertension, and unknown death) and three patients in the TACE alone group (post-procedural haemorrhage, ascites, and unknown death). No new safety signals were identified. INTERPRETATION: On-demand TACE plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab significantly improved TACE-PFS versus on-demand TACE alone. Overall survival follow-up is ongoing. FUNDING: Shanghai Roche Pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Stage II Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Upfront Surgery or Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy adoption in stage II non-small cell lung cancer is shrouded by lack of clear survival advantages and stratification across randomized clinical trials. METHODS: An individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis was conducted comparing overall survival of stage II patients (according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer TNM staging, eighth edition) receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in phase 3 randomized controlled trials with overall survival of patients undergoing upfront surgery included in the pathologic eighth and ninth edition TNM databases. Individual patient data were extracted using the individual patient data from Kaplan-Meier survival curves (IPDfromKM) method. Cox regression analyses estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and relative 95% (CIs). Meta-analysis and metaregression comparing neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy and chemotherapy were also conducted. Relative risk (RR) with 95% CI was derived. RESULTS: Overall survival IPD were extracted from 275 stage II patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy and from 6864 (eighth edition) and 7342 (ninth edition) patients undergoing upfront surgery in the pathologic TNM-database. Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy improved survival compared with upfront surgery in the eighth edition TNM database (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.53-0.87; P = .002) but yielded similar survival compared with the ninth edition (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.64-1.1; P = .10). Compared with chemotherapy, pathologic complete response (RR, 6.19; 95% CI, 3.37-10.27; P < .001) and major pathologic response (RR, 3.08; 95% CI, 2.27-4.16; P < .001) favored neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Similarly, chemoimmunotherapy improved event-free survival (HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.52-0.82; P 0.001) and overall survival (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50-0.92; P = .01). Similar rates of canceled surgery, open surgery, pneumonectomy, conversion from minimally invasive to open surgery, and positive margin were found. The percentage of stage II patients did not modulate surgical-related adverse events, 90-day mortality, and adjuvant treatment receipt. CONCLUSIONS: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy has encouraging results in stage II lung cancer, but stratification tools are warranted to select high-risk patients. Compared with chemotherapy, chemoimmunotherapy improves both long-term outcomes and pathologic response with comparable surgical outcomes.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Nivolumab plus Carboplatin and Paclitaxel in Patients with Locally Advanced Resectable Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck: A Phase II, Single-Arm Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: In locally advanced resectable squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN), patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy with major pathologic response (MPR) or pathologic complete response (pCR) have overall survival (OS) rates superior to those of patients with poorer pathologic responses. To improve efficacy, we added the PD-1 inhibitor nivolumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and evaluated the combination. PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-arm, open-label phase II trial, patients with newly diagnosed stage III to IV human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative SCCHN in the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx or stage II to III HPV-positive oropharyngeal SCCHN received neoadjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel (6 weeks) plus nivolumab (every other week), followed by surgery and adjuvant radiotherapy ± chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was pCR at the primary site. RESULTS: Thirty-four patients were enrolled and received neoadjuvant therapy. Thirty-three patients received surgery (R0 resection = 100%). Disease sites included the oral cavity (79%), oropharynx (12%), hypopharynx (6%), and larynx (3%). Twenty-eight (85%) patients had stage IVA disease. The median postsurgical follow-up was 35.3 months. Fourteen (41%) patients had grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events. Twenty-seven (82%) patients completed all cycles of neoadjuvant therapy. Twenty-four (73%) patients had at least an MPR at the primary site, and 15 (45%) had a pCR. In an unplanned analysis at 3 years, recurrence-free survival and OS were 74% and 83%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: This phase II trial of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel in previously untreated, locally advanced, resectable SCCHN was well tolerated and reached its primary endpoint of pCR at the primary site. A phase III confirmatory study is warranted in advanced-stage, resectable HPV-negative SCCHN. See related commentary by Anderson and Sikora, p. 4763.

articles.title: Multikinase Inhibition with Tinengotinib in Advanced Solid Tumors: Results from a Multicenter Phase Ib/II Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Tinengotinib, a multikinase inhibitor targeting Aurora kinases A/B, fibroblast growth factor receptors (FGFRs) 1 to 3, vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2, and Janus kinases 1 to 2, was evaluated in this phase Ib/II study to assess safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), efficacy, and genomic correlates of response and resistance in patients with advanced solid tumors. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors lacking standard treatment options were enrolled at 7 sites in the United States (NCT04742959). Tinengotinib was administered at 12 mg once daily in arm A and at multiple dose levels/dosing schedules in arm C. RESULTS: Among 197 patients receiving tinengotinib, treatment-related treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 160 (81.2%) patients, with hypertension being the most common. Hyperphosphatemia and ocular toxicities were uncommon. Clinical benefit was achieved by 43 of 159 (27.0%) evaluable patients, including 1 complete response, 20 partial responses, and 22 stable diseases ≥6 months. Antitumor activity was most pronounced with 10-mg and 12-mg dose levels. The objective response rates were 33.3%, 30%, and 13% in prostate cancer (n = 15), breast cancer (n = 20), and cholangiocarcinoma (n = 23), respectively. PK analyses supported the 10-mg once-daily regimen. Exploratory genomic analyses identified potential molecular correlations of response, including FGFR2 fusions in cholangiocarcinoma responders. Additional observations in breast cancer, including ROS1 alterations, were exploratory and should be considered hypothesis generating. Exploratory analyses also suggested associations between EGFR or MLL mutations in cholangiocarcinoma and MYC alterations in prostate cancer with shorter progression-free survival, consistent with emerging evidence linking MYC-driven lineage plasticity to androgen receptor-independent disease biology. Reductions in circulating tumor DNA variant allele frequency further supported pharmacodynamic target engagement. CONCLUSIONS: Tinengotinib demonstrated manageable toxicity with antitumor activity across advanced solid tumors, with infrequent hyperphosphatemia and ocular toxicities. Integrated PK-biomarker analyses support the continued clinical development of tinengotinib and the exploration of biomarker-informed precision oncology strategies.

articles.title: Spatial Organization of Tumor-Infiltrating B Cells Informs Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Response in Claudin 18.2-Expressing Gastric Cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2), a tight junction protein normally expressed in the gastric epithelium and rendered accessible during malignant transformation, has emerged as a key therapeutic target. Here, we seek to characterize the immune microenvironment of CLDN18.2-expressing gastric cancer and identify immune features associated with CLDN18.2 expression status. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: Tumor-immune features were profiled in 103 patients with HER2-neg/low advanced gastric cancer treated with first-line immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) using multiplex immunohistochemistry [7,423,483 cells across 2,315 regions of interest (ROI)]. The findings were validated in five published whole-transcriptome sequencing/microarray cohorts (1,521 samples), including the landmark CheckMate 649 phase III trial. Spatial immune architecture was assessed by cellular neighborhood analysis. Digital spatial profiling (DSP) was performed on 480 ROIs from a CLDN18.2-annotated tissue microarray (75 patients). RESULTS: CLDN18.2high tumors showed reproducible enrichment of humoral pathways, with higher CD20+ B-cell density and enrichment of B-cell/plasma-cell signatures. CLDN18.2 status alone was not associated with response or survival on first-line ICI therapy; in CLDN18.2low tumors, B-cell enrichment was associated with ICI benefit, unlike CLDN18.2high tumors. Spatial analyses indicated that CLDN18.2high tumors preferentially harbored tumor-infiltrating B cells, rather than tertiary lymphoid structure/lymphoid aggregate-like neighborhoods, and this tumor-compartment localization was associated with diminished ICI benefit. DSP confirmed that CD20+ B-cell enrichment was most pronounced within tumor regions, alongside compartment-specific activation of humoral and extrafollicular response programs and interferon-associated and remodeling signatures. CONCLUSIONS: CLDN18.2high gastric cancer exhibits a humoral-enriched microenvironment with increased tumor-infiltrating B cells and spatial immune organization associated with reduced ICI benefit. Spatial and humoral-state biomarkers may inform ongoing CLDN18.2-directed combination trials.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant Therapy in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: Current Evidence, Evolving Strategies, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Neoadjuvant therapy is now a cornerstone of muscle-invasive bladder cancer management, evolving from traditional cisplatin-based chemotherapy to novel immunotherapy and antibody-drug conjugate combinations. While dose-dense methotrexate, vinblastine, doxorubicin, and cisplatin remains the cytotoxic standard, the phase III NIAGARA and KEYNOTE 905 trials have established new benchmarks for cisplatin-eligible and ineligible populations, respectively. Furthermore, the integration of molecular subtyping, DNA damage repair biomarkers, and liquid biopsies (circulating tumor DNA) is facilitating a shift toward precision medicine. These advancements aim to optimize pathologic response, improve overall survival, and identify candidates for bladder-sparing approaches.

articles.title: Crizotinib versus observation or placebo for surgically resected early-stage ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group-American College of Radiology Imaging Network E4512): a phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Crizotinib is an established first-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibitor approved for the treatment of advanced ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). E4512 aimed to evaluate the effect of adjuvant crizotinib on disease-free survival (DFS) in patients with resected, early-stage ALK-positive NSCLC. METHODS: In this randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial conducted in 1618 sites across the USA, Guam, and Puerto Rico, patients were randomly assigned 1:1 by computer-generated sequence to receive crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily or observation (changed from initial double-blind placebo) for up 2 years. Eligible patients had resected NSCLC tumours that were 4 cm or larger in diameter or lymph node-positive, negative surgical margins, no neoadjuvant therapy, ALK positivity by local or central testing, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1. Adjuvant chemotherapy was allowed but not required. Stratification factors were stage, previous radiation therapy, and sex. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival (DFS) in the centrally tested ALK-positive intention-to-treat population and presented as hazard ratio with 90% and 95% CI. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02201992) and is completed. Safety was assessed in all patients whose tumours tested ALK-positive and who received the study drug. FINDINGS: Between Aug 18, 2014, and May 10, 2024, 166 patients (of 168 planned) were enrolled (85 to crizotinib and 81 to observation). Accrual was stopped when the US Food and Drug Administration approved adjuvant alectinib for resected ALK-positive NSCLC. Overall, 153 (92%) patients had centrally confirmed ALK-positive tumours. Among these 153 individuals, 99 (65%) were female, 54 (35%) were male, and 121 (79%) were White. After a median follow-up of 65·7 months (IQR 37·5-85·6), median DFS was 74·6 (95% CI 71·2 to not assessable) months in the crizotinib group and 75·1 (64·7 to NA) months in the observation group (HR 1·08 [90% CI 0·67-1·73; 95% CI 0·61-1·90; p=0·80). In the crizotinib group, 46 (58%) patients had grade 3 or higher adverse events of any attribution (most commonly diarrhoea, in eight [10%] patients; oedema, in four [5%] patients; and hypertension, in four [5%] patients), including one death that was not deemed treatment-related. 21 (27%) patients had serious adverse events, most commonly dyspnoea (three [4%] patients), abdominal pain (two [3%] patients), thromboembolic event (two [3%] patients), diarrhoea (two [3%] patients), dehydration (two [3%] patients), and hypertension (two [3%] patients). INTERPRETATION: Adjuvant crizotinib does not prolong DFS in patients with surgically resected ALK-positive NSCLC. These findings suggest that crizotinib should not be recommended as an adjuvant therapy for patients with resected ALK-positive NSCLC. FUNDING: National Cancer Institute of the US National Institutes of Health.

articles.title: Tinzaparin Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Cancer: A Comparative Modeling Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CAT) is common and a leading cause of mortality in patients with cancer. In specific CAT scenarios, low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWHs), including tinzaparin, are preferred over direct oral anticoagulants. Despite the importance of understanding LMWH pharmacokinetics (PK) in cancer for optimizing CAT management, available data remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To compare tinzaparin PK in cancer and non-cancer patients by developing a population PK model. METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, case-: control trial enrolled patients receiving once-daily subcutaneous tinzaparin at a therapeutic dose of 175 IU·kg RESULTS: A total of 333 patients (including 46 matched cancer and non-cancer patients) were included in the analysis. A monocompartmental model with first-order absorption best described tinzaparin PK. The volume of distribution was associated with body weight, while clearance and anti-Xa activity were associated with creatinine clearance. No significant differences were observed between matched cancer and non-cancer patients in anti-Xa activity exposure at day 1 and steady state. CONCLUSION: PK profiles were comparable between cancer and non-cancer patients. Additionally, further studies should clarify the role of renal function in guiding tinzaparin dosing.

articles.title: Daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma: MAIA final survival analysis.
articles.abstract: In previous analyses of MAIA, daratumumab plus lenalidomide/dexamethasone (D-Rd) significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival (OS) versus lenalidomide/dexamethasone (Rd) in transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM). We report results on long-term OS and subsequent antimyeloma therapies from the MAIA final analysis. A protocol amendment (July 20, 2021) led to a long-term extension of MAIA, during which patients were followed for OS. A total of 737 patients were randomized to D-Rd (n = 368) or Rd (n = 369). At a median follow-up of 89.3 months (range, 0.0-102.2; interquartile range, 85.3-93.0), median OS was 90.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 80.8-not estimable [NE]) with D-Rd versus 64.1 months (56.0-70.8) with Rd (hazard ratio [HR], 0.67; 95% CI, 0.55-0.82); estimated 7-year OS rates were 53.1% (95% CI, 47.8-58.2) and 39.3% (34.1-44.5), respectively. Median time to subsequent antimyeloma treatment was not reached (95% CI, 84.1-NE) for D-Rd versus 42.4 months (33.5-50.6) for Rd (HR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.41-0.63; P < 0.0001). Death due to adverse events occurred in 84 patients (D-Rd, n = 44/364 [12%]; Rd, n = 40/365 [11%]). With >7 years of follow-up, D-Rd demonstrated a new benchmark for median OS (7.5 years) in transplant-ineligible NDMM, further supporting frontline D-Rd use to maximize survival.

articles.title: Phase III Trials Test First-Line Options in Advanced NSCLC.
articles.abstract: Presented at the 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer, two phase III trials-PAPILLON and REZILIENT3-established amivantamab and zipalertinib combination therapies as effective first-line strategies for advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertions, with significantly improved progression-free survival, although high crossover rates prevented them demonstrating an overall survival benefit. Separately, HARMONi-2 showed that the bispecific antibody ivonescimab improved overall survival versus pembrolizumab in PD-L1-positive NSCLC, supporting its use as standard of care in China while larger global trials continue.

articles.title: [Update on ovarian cancer].
articles.abstract: The high value of surgery aimed at macroscopic complete resection is undisputed. The TRUST trial (Trial of Radical Upfront Surgical Therapy) aimed to determine the ideal timing of surgery (primary vs. interval debulking). While a significant progression-free survival benefit for primary surgery was demonstrated, the overall survival benefit was only numerical and not statistically significant. Based on the TRUST trial, primary surgery should still be recommended if macroscopic complete resection can be achieved with acceptable morbidity. Careful patient selection at specialized centers is crucial. A milestone in the systemic treatment of advanced ovarian cancer is the option of maintenance therapy with bevacizumab, poly(adenosine diphosphate-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, or the combination of olaparib plus bevacizumab. Biomarker testing, specifically BRCA and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) testing, is essential for treatment selection. In case of recurrence, where platinum-based chemotherapy is an option, platinum-containing combination chemotherapy should be administered, and the use of maintenance therapy should be considered. If platinum is not an option, three phase III trials have fortunately now demonstrated a significant overall survival benefit with the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV) in patients with high α‑folate receptor expression (MIRASOL trial), or with pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel ± bevacizumab in patients with CPS ≥ 1 (KEYNOTE-B96 trial), as well as with relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel (ROSELLA trial), each compared to standard chemotherapy. MIRV and Pembrolizumab are already approved. The increasingly complex treatment of ovarian cancer should therefore be carried out in specialized German Cancer Society (DKG)-certified gynecological cancer centers as an effective tool for quality improvement. Der hohe Stellenwert der Operation mit dem Ziel der makroskopischen Komplettresektion ist unstrittig. In der TRUST (Trial of Radical Upfront Surgical Therapy)-Studie sollte der ideale Operationszeitpunkt (Primär- vs. Intervall-Debulking) geklärt werden. Es zeigte sich hier ein signifikanter Benefit für das progressionsfreie Überleben bei Primäroperation, aber nur ein numerischer, nicht signifikanter Gesamtüberlebensvorteil. Auf Grundlage der TRUST-Studie sollte weiterhin eine Primäroperation empfohlen werden, wenn bei vertretbarer Morbidität eine Primäroperation mit makroskopischer Komplettresektion ermöglicht werden kann. Eine gute Selektionierung der Patientinnen an ausgewiesenen Zentren ist entscheidend. Meilenstein in der Systemtherapie des fortgeschrittenen Ovarialkarzinoms ist die Option der Erhaltungstherapie mit Bevacizumab, PARP („poly adenosine diphosphate-ribose polymerase“)-Inhibitoren oder der Kombination von Olaparib plus Bevacizumab. Biomarkertestungen im Sinne von BRCA- und HRD („homologous recombination deficiency“)-Testung sind für die Auswahl entscheidend. Im Falle eines Rezidivs, bei dem Platin eine Option darstellt, sollten platinhaltige Kombinationschemotherapien appliziert und der Einsatz einer Erhaltungstherapie geprüft werden. Wenn Platin keine Option ist, zeigten nun erfreulicherweise drei Phase-III-Studien einen signifikanten Gesamtüberlebensvorteil mit dem ADC  (Antikörper-Wirkstoff-Konjugat) Mirvetuximab Soravtansin (MIRV) bei Folatrezeptor α high (Mirasol-Studie) oder mit Pembrolizumab plus Paclitaxel ± Bevacizumab bei CPS ≥ 1 (KEYNOTE-B96-Studie), aber auch für Relacorilant plus nab-Paclitaxel (ROSELLA-Studie) jeweils im Vergleich zu Standardchemotherapien. MIRV und Pembrolizumab sind bereits zugelassen. Die immer komplexer werdende Therapie des Ovarialkarzinoms sollte daher in spezialisierten DKG (Deutsche Krebsgesellschaft)-zertifizierten Gynäkologischen Krebszentren als ein wirksames Instrument zur Qualitätsverbesserung erfolgen.

articles.title: Trastuzumab Botidotin Versus Trastuzumab Emtansine in Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer: A Phase III, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of the novel human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate, trastuzumab botidotin, for the treatment of HER2-positive unresectable/metastatic breast cancer (BC). METHODS: In this phase III, open-label, multicenter trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06968585), conducted at 57 centers in China, adult patients with HER2-positive, unresectable/metastatic BC who had received prior trastuzumab and a taxane were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive trastuzumab botidotin or trastuzumab emtansine. The primary end point was progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), using an intention-to-treat analysis. In a prespecified interim analysis of PFS per BICR, trastuzumab botidotin met the prespecified superiority boundary ( RESULTS: Between July 18, 2023, and April 26, 2024, 365 patients were randomly assigned to trastuzumab botidotin (n = 182) or trastuzumab emtansine (n = 183). At data cutoff (median follow-up, 14.9 months), trastuzumab botidotin resulted in longer PFS than trastuzumab emtansine (median, 11.1 CONCLUSION: Among patients with HER2-positive advanced BC previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane, trastuzumab botidotin resulted in significantly longer PFS than trastuzumab emtansine, with a distinct safety profile.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology

articles.title: PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies in solid tumors: clinical trial updates from ASCO 2026.
articles.abstract: PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies integrate immune checkpoint blockade and VEGF inhibition within a single molecule, offering a potential strategy to overcome angiogenesis-associated immune resistance. At the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, the randomized phase 3 HARMONi-6 trial demonstrated an overall survival benefit with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy over tislelizumab plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), extending survival evidence to an active PD-1-based first-line comparator. Exploratory phase 2 studies of pumitamig, SSGJ-707, and HB0025 reported encouraging activity in first-line NSCLC, while phase 1 and 2 studies of IMM2510 and ivonescimab-based regimens suggested activity after prior immunotherapy. Smaller exploratory studies also reported activity in perioperative head and neck cancer, colorectal cancer, endometrial cancer, and mucosal melanoma. Collectively, these findings highlight the clinical potential of PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies, with the strongest evidence in first-line squamous NSCLC and broader applications remaining hypothesis-generating. Future development should prioritize predictive biomarkers, resistance mechanisms, optimal treatment sequencing, and careful assessment of immune-related and VEGF-associated toxicities.

articles.title: Two-year outcomes following PSMA PET and MRI guided prostate SABR with simultaneous focal boost: a brief report from the ARGOS-CLIMBER phase 1/2 trial.
articles.abstract: ARGOS-CLIMBER is a phase 1/2 trial evaluating PSMA PET and MRI guided prostate SABR with a simultaneous boost to intraprostatic and nodal disease in men with unfavourable intermediate and high-risk prostate cancer. The updated results demonstrate acceptable safety and quality of life with high biochemical and imaging response rates.
articles.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology

articles.title: Neoadjuvant antibody-drug conjugates for early-stage breast cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathologic complete response (pCR) is a key endpoint of neoadjuvant therapy in early-stage breast cancer (EBC), associated with improved survival, particularly in triple-negative and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive disease. More recently, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), established in metastatic disease, are being evaluated in the neoadjuvant setting. DESIGN: We systematically searched for studies of EBC patients treated with neoadjuvant ADCs, alone or in combination. Meta-analyses were carried out using a random-effects model, with heterogeneity assessed via I² statistics and Cochran's Q test. RESULTS: Twenty-four studies were included, 22 (2363 patients) contributed to the pCR analysis, predominantly phase I/II trials and two phase III studies. Nine ADCs targeting HER2, trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2), LIV1 or human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3), and incorporating six distinct payload classes were identified. The pooled pCR rate was 38.34% (95% CI 29.36-47.72; I² = 92.8%), highest among hormone receptor (HR)-negative/HER2 + tumors (65.06%), followed by HR+/HER2 + (47.53%), TNBC (29.37%), and HR+/HER2 - (2.94%) (p < 0.0001). By target, pCR rates were 43.93% for HER2-directed ADCs, 41.41% for TROP2, 16.57% for LIV1, and 3% for HER3. Common all-grade adverse events (AEs) included nausea (64.52%), diarrhea (48.24%), alopecia (39.19%), alanine aminotransferase elevation (38.80%), aspartate aminotransferase elevation (34.87%), neutropenia (29.53%), vomiting (25.95%), and anemia (24.89%). Grade ≥ 3 AEs occurred in 25.06% of patients. CONCLUSION: Neoadjuvant ADC-based strategies yield clinically meaningful pCR rates in EBC, with the greatest benefit in HER2 + disease, supporting further investigation and biomarker-guided patient selection.

articles.title: Decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide versus busulfan-cyclophosphamide myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for reducing risk of relapse in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia in China: an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: An unmet need persists for optimal myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia. We investigated whether decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide (DAC-BuCy) conditioning reduced the risk of relapse compared with busulfan-cyclophosphamide (BuCy) conditioning. METHODS: In this open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at eight transplantation centres in China, eligible patients were aged 14-65 years, had morphologically confirmed KMT2A-rearranged leukaemia, and had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) before HSCT to DAC-BuCy (intravenous decitabine 20 mg/m FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2019, and Jan 31, 2023, 130 patients were randomised to receive a DAC-BuCy (n=65; 34 [52%] female and 31 [48%] male) or BuCy (n=65; 29 [45%] female and 36 [55%] male) regimen. Median follow-up was 34·7 months (IQR 30·2-52·5). 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 12% (95% CI 6-22) in the DAC-BuCy group and 29% (19-41) in the BuCy group (hazard ratio 0·41 [0·20-0·87]; p=0·017). The most common grade 3-5 adverse events were infections or infestations (DAC-BuCy group 27 [42%] and BuCy group 25 [38%]), acute graft-versus-host disease (DAC-BuCy group 23 [35%] and BuCy group 22 [34%]), and gastrointestinal disorders (DAC-BuCy group 14 [22%] and BuCy group 15 [23%]). Four (6%) patients in the DAC-BuCy group and five (8%) patients in the BuCy group died from adverse events, of which two were due to regimen-related toxicities: one nervous system disorder in the DAC-BuCy group and one cardiac disorder in the BuCy group. INTERPRETATION: The addition of decitabine to BuCy conditioning reduced the risk of relapse with an acceptable safety profile in adult patients with KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia and could be a suitable therapeutic option for this population. FUNDING: The National Natural Science Foundation of China, the National Key Research and Development Program of China, the Science and Technology Program of Guangdong Province, the Non-communicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, the Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province, the Science and Technology Planning Project of Guangzhou, and the Outstanding Youth Cultivation Program of Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University. TRANSLATION: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Diabetes and Performance Status Predict Severe, Persistent Radiation Proctitis: Long-Term Endoscopic Findings From STELLAR Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize the long-term endoscopic natural history of chronic radiation proctitis (CRP) and identify predictors of severe lesions in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer from the STELLAR study (NCT02533271) . METHODS AND MATERIALS: This secondary analysis included 74 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer undergoing anal-preserving surgery after neoadjuvant therapy (39: short-course radiation therapy/total neoadjuvant therapy [TNT] and 35: long-course chemoradiation therapy [CRT]). Systematic endoscopic follow-up (>2 years) was performed, with mucosal damage graded by the Vienna Rectoscopy Score (VRS). Multivariate analyses identified factors for severe (VRS ≥3) and persistent severe CRP. RESULTS: The incidence of VRS ≥3 CRP was 33.3% (TNT) versus 20.0% (CRT) (P = .197). Endoscopic severity peaked at 2 years after radiation. A distinct recovery trend was observed in the TNT group, but not in the CRT group. Diabetes mellitus was an independent risk factor for both severe CRP (hazard ratio [HR], 5.46; 95% CI, 1.25-23.89; P = .024) and persistent severe CRP (HR, 6.09; 95% CI, 1.23-30.23; P = .027). Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 1 predicted persistent severe CRP (HR, 8.81; 95% CI, 1.50-51.68; P = .016). DISCUSSION: Hypofractionated radiation therapy (TNT) did not increase severe CRP risk and showed a favorable recovery pattern. Diabetes and reduced performance status are strong, independent predictors of severe and persistent endoscopic injury, enabling risk-stratified patient management. These findings support tailored surveillance and preventive strategies for high-risk individuals.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics

articles.title: Nurse-led attribution remodeling training based on the Neuman systems model to enhance resilience, adaptive coping, and attributional style in women newly diagnosed with breast cancer: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological interventions for patients with breast cancer often overlook the critical role of maladaptive attributional style in shaping their adjustment. Therefore, the need for theory-driven, scalable interventions that target cognitive restructuring, particularly during the vulnerable post-diagnosis period, is clear.
