articles.title: Primed to feel, not to flare: Early life adversity and psychological sensitivity to interleukin-6 in a randomized trial among middle-aged female breast cancer survivors.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: There have been recent calls to investigate potential moderators of inflammation's psychological effects in humans. In a small observational study, Kuhlman et al. (2020b) found that individuals with higher early life adversity (ELA) showed heightened psychological sensitivity (i.e., more depressed mood and poorer cognition but not decreased social connection) in response to influenza vaccine-induced increases in interleukin-6 (IL-6). In a larger cohort with a placebo-controlled experimental design, we examined ELA's moderating effects on (1) vaccine-induced IL-6 reactivity, (2) increases in IL-6 reactivity and psychological outcomes, and (3) the effect of injection type on psychological outcomes. METHOD: Female breast cancer survivors (N = 172) received the typhoid vaccine and saline placebo injection in a randomized sequence at two separate visits. At screening, early life adversity was indexed using two measures: the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form and the Kessler Childhood Adversity Index. During each visit, IL-6 was measured six times over 7.5 h, and psychological outcomes (sadness, focus difficulty, memory difficulty, social connection) were repeatedly assessed across 8.5 h. RESULTS: Neither ELA index moderated vaccine-induced IL-6 reactivity (ps > 0.17) nor moderated the effect of injection type on psychological outcomes (ps > 0.25). Instead, those with more ELA had greater psychological sensitivity to inflammatory increases. Among individuals with higher ELA exposure (≥2 adverse events), increases in IL-6 were associated with greater sadness (p = 0.030) and focus difficulty (p = 0.048), marginally greater memory difficulty (p = 0.067), but were unrelated to feelings of social connection (ps > 0.81). These associations were nonsignificant among individuals who reported zero or one adverse event. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that among individuals with greater exposure to early life adversity, those with heightened inflammatory reactivity may be particularly vulnerable to IL-6's psychological effects, highlighting a potential target for identifying and supporting individuals at risk for inflammation-associated depression.

articles.title: Hypofractionated 44 Gy in 20 fractions versus conventional chemoradiation in cervical cancer: 2-year results of the randomized HYPOCx-iRex trial with an exploratory pooled analysis of a single-institute EMBRACE-II cohort.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate 2-year late gastrointestinal (GI) toxicity, oncologic outcomes, and cost-effectiveness of hypofractionated concurrent chemoradiation with 44 Gy in 20 fractions (44 Gy/20F; HYPO) versus conventional fractionation (45 Gy/25F; CVRT + EMB) for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). METHODS: The primary analysis was the randomized HYPOCx-iRex comparison (HYPO n = 21 vs. CVRT n = 19). A pre-planned pooled analysis additionally incorporated a concurrent, nonrandomized single-institute EMBRACE-II cohort (EMB n = 28; total n = 68). Late GI toxicity was graded by CTCAEv5.0. Dose-toxicity analysis used Cox and Probit regression to identify the effective dose associated with 10% toxicity probability (ED10). The indirect ratio of excess dose volume at 60 Gy EQD2 (iRex60) was evaluated as a brachytherapy (BT) conformity index. Locoregional control (LRC) and overall survival (OS) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were calculated from provider and societal perspectives. RESULTS: Median overall treatment time was 39 versus 46 days in HYPO versus CVRT+EMB (p < 0.001). Late GI toxicity was numerically higher in HYPO (2-year Gr ≥2: 23.8% vs. 10.8%, pLR = 0.168; Gr ≥3: 19.1% vs. 5.3%, pLR = 0.066); iRex60 was identified as an independent predictor in multivariable regression (ED10 = 1.6 and 1.85 for Gr ≥2/Gr ≥3; proposed cut-off iRex60 <1.7). Favorable but nonsignificant trends in LRC (95.2% vs. 77.5%; HR = 0.43, pLR = 0.260) and OS (100% vs. 76.8%; HR = 0.22, pLR = 0.107) were observed. The 44Gy/20F regimen demonstrated dominant cost-effectiveness. CONCLUSION: Hypofractionated chemoradiation achieved LRC and OS comparable to conventional fractionation with shorter treatment time and lower cost. The higher late GI toxicity observed with hypofractionation is clinically meaningful without statistical significance. Further optimization of brachytherapy conformity and low-to-intermediate dose constraints is proposed before clinical adoption. The iRex60 threshold and the cost-effectiveness findings are hypothesis-generating and need further validation.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.

articles.title: Biomarker-guided treatment selection in metastatic colorectal cancer: A critical review of established and emerging therapies.
articles.abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is increasingly managed according to mismatch repair status and actionable molecular alterations. In this structured narrative review, we separately examine mismatch repair-deficient/microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) and microsatellite-stable/mismatch repair-proficient (MSS/pMMR) disease and distinguish established treatments from investigational strategies. In dMMR/MSI-H mCRC, immune checkpoint inhibition is the established first-line standard, with pembrolizumab and nivolumab plus ipilimumab producing durable disease control. In MSS/pMMR mCRC, tumor molecular findings guide targeted therapy. For BRAF V600E-mutant disease, encorafenib plus cetuximab with fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy is a first-line standard. HER2-directed therapy with tucatinib plus trastuzumab or trastuzumab deruxtecan and combined KRAS G12C and EGFR inhibition are established after prior treatment but are not approved in the first-line setting. Across MMR subgroups, rare NTRK or RET fusions can confer eligibility for tumor-agnostic TRK or RET inhibition, although CRC-specific cohorts remain small. In previously treated non-MSI-H/dMMR mCRC, STELLAR-303 was the first phase 3 trial to demonstrate a significant overall survival benefit with an immune checkpoint inhibitor-containing regimen, zanzalintinib plus atezolizumab. Other investigational strategies include additional immunotherapy combinations, EGFR-MET bispecific antibody therapy with amivantamab, T-cell-engaging bispecific antibodies, therapeutic cancer vaccines, cellular therapies, and microbiome-directed approaches. For each therapeutic class, we summarize the supporting evidence, define its place in the treatment sequence, and identify the remaining evidence gaps.

articles.title: Robot-assisted gastrectomy for locally advanced gastric cancer and complex clinical scenarios: technical evolution, evidence gaps, and future directions.
articles.abstract: Robot-assisted gastrectomy has evolved over two decades from a technical curiosity into a feasible operative option, but its role in locally advanced gastric cancer and complex clinical scenarios remains unsettled. This narrative review is based on a documented search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (January 2002 through September 2026) and synthesizes evidence on technical evolution, perioperative and oncological outcomes, and the use of robotic platforms in obesity, advanced age, high comorbidity burden, post-neoadjuvant fibrosis, and total gastrectomy with esophagojejunostomy. Most comparative evidence is observational (propensity-matched and single-center), and evidence for advanced or complex disease is partly extrapolated from early-stage and mixed-stage cohorts. Robotic gastrectomy is associated consistently with less blood loss and, in some series, higher lymph node yields at anatomically demanding stations, whereas operative time is longer, overall complication rates are generally similar, and no adequately powered randomized trial has shown a survival advantage. One randomized phase II trial in distal gastrectomy met a non-inferiority criterion for 3-year disease-free survival; an exploratory survival difference in that trial and observational signals of improved recurrence-free survival in stage III disease remain hypothesis-generating. High-quality patient-reported and functional outcomes, and data from non-East Asian populations, are scarce. Higher costs, a learning curve of approximately 25-50 cases, and the absence of phase III superiority data temper broad endorsement. Single-port systems, alternative platforms, and artificial-intelligence and augmented-reality tools are emerging but are not yet validated in gastric cancer surgery. We map each claim to its source population, distinguish direct from extrapolated evidence, and identify the trial designs and patient-centered endpoints needed to define the appropriate role of robotic gastrectomy.

articles.title: Subtyping limited stage small cell lung cancer (LS SCLC) reveals inflammatory subtypes with improved chemoradiotherapy outcomes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) remains the primary treatment for limited stage (LS) small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Although most patients respond, the majority relapse and die from the disease, and treatment-related toxicity is common. Molecular subtyping has been extensively investigated in SCLC, but its clinical relevance remains uncertain, and most studies have focused on systemic treatment of extensive-stage SCLC. We analysed baseline tumor samples from a subset of participants (n = 77) in a randomized trial (n = 170) comparing high-dose (60 Gy/40 fractions) with standard-dose (45 Gy/30 fractions) twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy given concurrently with platinum-etoposide chemotherapy for LS SCLC, aiming to characterize molecular subtypes of LS SCLC and evaluate their association with time to progression (TTP) and overall survival (OS). METHODS: Molecular subtypes were defined in 81 samples using non-negative matrix factorization on gene expression data, supported by differential expression and known SCLC markers. RESULTS: Inflamed subtypes were associated with better treatment outcomes. Univariable analysis indicate that SCLC-I-NE (inflamed neuroendocrine) was associated with longer TTP (HR 0.10, 95 % CI 0.01-0.80, p = 0.03), and SCLC-I-nNE (inflamed non-neuroendocrine) was associated with improved OS (HR 0.16, 95 % CI 0.03-0.77, p = 0.02). By contrast, SCLC-N (NEUROD1-driven) was consistently associated with both shorter TTP (HR 6.90, 95 % CI 1.49-31.92, p = 0.01) and OS (HR 4.89, 95 % CI 1.24-19.21, p = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: For LS SCLC patients receiving CRT, tumors of inflamed subtypes were associated with improved outcomes, whereas SCLC-N tumors were linked to unfavorable TTP and OS.

articles.title: Advanced Anal Squamous Cell Carcinoma in the Chemoimmunotherapy Era: Retifanlimab, Nivolumab, and a Practical Framework for Treatment Selection.
articles.abstract: Advanced anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is a rare human papillomavirus-associated malignancy with historically limited prospective evidence for systemic therapy. InterAAct established carboplatin-paclitaxel as a clinically favorable chemotherapy backbone compared with cisplatin-fluorouracil. POD1UM-303/InterAACT-2 subsequently showed that adding retifanlimab significantly improved progression-free survival in patients with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease. At the final overall-survival analysis, median overall survival was 32.8 versus 22.2 months (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.55-1.01); the regimen has received regulatory authorization in the United States, the European Union, and Japan. EA2176 is evaluating carboplatin-paclitaxel with or without nivolumab and will clarify whether first-line PD-1-based chemoimmunotherapy represents a reproducible class effect. This focused narrative review critically summarizes the evidence for retifanlimab- and nivolumab-based strategies and proposes a practical framework for treatment selection. Key considerations include performance status, immune-checkpoint-inhibitor eligibility, HIV infection, autoimmune risk, neuropathy, organ function, tumor burden, local symptom control, and post-chemoimmunotherapy sequencing. Retifanlimab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel currently has the most mature phase III evidence, whereas nivolumab-based chemoimmunotherapy remains investigational pending EA2176. Treatment decisions should distinguish phase III-validated options from class-effect extrapolation and integrate multidisciplinary local therapy when appropriate.

articles.title: Comparison of Postoperative Pain Following Modified Radical Mastectomy under Thoracic Epidural Anesthesia versus General Anesthesia: A Randomized Control Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast surgeries are commonly performed under general anesthesia. The aim of the study was to compare postoperative pain following modified radical mastectomy under thoracic epidural anesthesia versus general anesthesia with the use of laryngeal mask airway. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This randomized controlled study was performed on hundred patients undergoing unilateral modified radical mastectomy. The patients were assigned into two equal groups, E and G. Group E patients received thoracic epidural anaesthesia, and group G received general anesthesia. The primary objective was to compare postoperative pain scores between the two groups. Secondary objectives included incidence of postoperative sore throat, hoarseness of voice, cough, nausea and vomiting, perioperative analgesic requirement, patient and surgeon satisfaction, duration of hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and any associated anesthesia complications. RESULTS: Both groups were similar with respect to demographics. Postoperative pain score was significantly lower in Group E at all time points. The perioperative analgesic requirement was significantly higher in Group G than in Group E, and this was statistically significant with P < 0.001. Duration of hospital stay and intraoperative hemodynamics were comparable between the two groups. Patient satisfaction was significantly higher in Group G; however, surgeons were satisfied with both methods. Sore throat, cough, hoarseness of voice, nausea and vomiting, and duration of ICU stay were significantly higher in group G. Infiltration of local anesthetic in the axilla was required in 10% of the patients in the epidural group. CONCLUSIONS: Although patients found general anesthesia more satisfying, thoracic epidural anesthesia provided significantly better postoperative analgesia compared with general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway inpatients undergoing modified radical mastectomy and was associated with significantly lower ICU stay, comparable surgeon satisfaction with lower incidence of postoperative sore throat, nausea and vomiting, hoarseness of voice, and cough. CONTEXTE:: Les chirurgies du sein sont couramment réalisées sous anesthésie générale. Le but de cette étude était de comparer la douleur postopératoire après une mastectomie radicale modifiée sous anesthésie péridurale thoracique par rapport à l’anesthésie générale avec utilisation d’un masque laryngé. MATÉRIEL ET MÉTHODES:: Cette étude randomisée et contrôlée a été réalisée sur cent patientes subissant une mastectomie radicale modifiée unilatérale. Les patientes ont été réparties en deux groupes égaux, E et G. Les patientes du groupe E ont reçu une anesthésie péridurale thoracique, et celles du groupe G une anesthésie générale. L’objectif principal était de comparer les scores de douleur postopératoire entre les deux groupes. Les objectifs secondaires comprenaient l’incidence des maux de gorge postopératoires, de l’enrouement de la voix, de la toux, des nausées et vomissements, des besoins en analgésiques peropératoires, de la satisfaction de la patiente et du chirurgien, de la durée du séjour à l’hôpital et en unité de soins intensifs (USI), ainsi que de toute complication anesthésique associée. RÉSULTATS:: Les deux groupes étaient similaires en ce qui concerne les données démographiques.1 Le score de douleur postopératoire était significativement plus faible dans le Groupe E à tous les moments. Le besoin en analgésiques peropératoires était significativement plus élevé dans le Groupe G que dans le Groupe E, et cela était statistiquement significatif avec $ CONCLUSIONS:: Bien que les patientes aient trouvé l’anesthésie générale plus satisfaisante, l’anesthésie péridurale thoracique a procuré une analgésie postopératoire significativement meilleure par rapport à l’anesthésie générale avec masque laryngé chez les patientes subissant une mastectomie radicale modifiée, et était associée à une durée de séjour en USI significativement plus courte, à une satisfaction du chirurgien comparable avec une incidence plus faible des maux de gorge postopératoires, des nausées et vomissements, de l’enrouement de la voix et de la toux.

articles.title: A Trial-Level Benefit-Toxicity Mapping Framework for Adjuvant Therapy in Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Focused Review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adjuvant systemic therapy for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) has evolved from vascular endothelial growth factor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (VEGF-TKIs) to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and emerging combination strategies. However, the interpretation of adjuvant trial results requires consideration not only of disease-free survival (DFS) benefit but also of severe toxicity, treatment discontinuation, comparator structure, and trial risk composition. METHODS: We conducted a focused review of randomized Phase III adjuvant RCC trials identified through PubMed and prespecified publicly available trial reports. Peer-reviewed trials were included in the primary evidence set, and contemporary conference reports were incorporated as an exploratory update. Trial-level data were extracted for efficacy, grade ≥ 3 adverse events (AEs), AE-driven and patient-initiated treatment discontinuation, and protocol-defined risk composition. A descriptive benefit-toxicity mapping framework was used to visualize DFS benefit, treatment-limiting toxicity, severe AE burden, and high-risk patient proportion without implying indirect treatment ranking. RESULTS: Nine peer-reviewed trial programs and one conference-only report were included. TKI-based trials showed limited and inconsistent DFS benefit, with only S-TRAC meeting its primary endpoint, while grade ≥ 3 AE burden was consistently high (60%-72%) and patient-initiated discontinuation was frequent. Among ICI-based trials, KEYNOTE-564 showed DFS benefit, whereas IMmotion010 and CheckMate 914 Part A were negative. RAMPART (conference report) and LITESPARK-022 showed additional DFS signals with ICI-based combinations, accompanied by AE-driven discontinuation in approximately one-third of patients, with important differences in risk composition and comparator design. CONCLUSIONS: Trial-level benefit-toxicity mapping contextualizes adjuvant RCC trials by integrating DFS benefit, toxicity burden, treatment-limiting events, and risk composition, without implying direct cross-trial ranking.
articles.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association

articles.title: Methyl aminolevulinate-PpIX mediated fluorescence-guided mapping of high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: a pilot prospective clinical trial (PhotoDiVin).
articles.abstract: The worldwide prevalence of vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is increasing and is characterized by the high risk of recurrence and evolution towards vulvar cancer. Positive margins following surgical excision are the most important criteria of recurrence risk. We conducted a pilot clinical study to assess the fluorescence-based cartography of VIN lesions using methyl aminolevulinate (m-ALA), which is a prodrug of the fluorophore protoporphyrin IX (PpIX). A prospective, single-center, single-arm clinical trial included 17 women with histologically confirmed high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (dVIN or vHSIL). Following topical methyl aminolevulinate application, fluorescence-guided examination under 405-nm light was performed. Targeted biopsies from fluorescent and non-fluorescent areas were compared with histopathology to assess concordance and the ability of fluorescence to accurately identify high-grade lesions. Among 34 biopsies, histopathological findings were concordant with fluorescence in 91% of cases. The procedure correctly identified intraepithelial neoplasia areas in 14 patients, yielding a success rate of 82% (95%CI 56-96%). Sensitivity and specificity were 93% (95%CI 68-100%) and 89% (95%CI 67-99%), respectively. The tolerance of the procedure was excellent with no pain and no side effects neither after cream application nor after illumination. This pilot study suggests that fluorescence imaging is a workable technique to mark VIN lesions with m-ALA cream. Further studies are needed to improve the reproducibility and ease of use of this method.

articles.title: Trial-specific absolute disease-free survival effects of postoperative PD-1/PD-L1 blockade after complete resection of NSCLC: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Postoperative PD-1/PD-L1 blockade after complete resection of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is mainly reported using relative disease-free survival (DFS) effects. We estimated absolute effects for distinct completed trial policies. METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized phase III trials of postoperative single-agent PD-1/PD-L1 blockade. Published Kaplan-Meier curves were reconstructed to estimate trial-specific 36-month restricted mean DFS time (RMST) and DFS probability differences. Primary intervals used 2,000 arm-stratified bootstrap replicates. Sensitivity analyses examined reconstruction methods and time horizons; overall survival (OS) reconstruction was exploratory. Harms were described by trial, without pooling. REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261469971. RESULTS: Four trial families included 4,336 participants. Thirty-six-month RMST differences ranged from 1.34 to 1.97 months; DFS probability differences corresponded to 2.3-6.1 additional participants without a trial-defined DFS event per 100 randomized. Confidence intervals included zero for two RMST and three DFS probability estimates. The KEYNOTE-091 DFS probability interval crossed zero under alternative reconstruction; RMST interval interpretations were unchanged. The four-trial hazard-ratio synthesis was descriptive and model sensitive. Exploratory 36-month OS reconstructions in three trials yielded intervals allowing benefit and harm. In three trials with available between-arm safety data, severe and serious adverse events were more frequent with checkpoint blockade. CONCLUSIONS: Reconstructed trial-specific estimates suggest average absolute DFS gains through 36 months, with substantial uncertainty. They complement the original trial results when discussing postoperative treatment; they do not establish a class-wide effect, treatment ranking, or individual benefit.

articles.title: Repurposing marimastat as a broad-spectrum small-molecule inhibitor for snakebite envenoming: From oncology trials to the development of field-ready interventions.
articles.abstract: Marimastat is a pan-catalytic MMP inhibitor that is emerging as an alternative therapy for venom bite lesions because it can antagonise metalloproteinases in snake venom, without being constrained by the production or storage requirements of antivenoms or intravenous administration. Metalloproteinases are important effector enzymes in many aspects of tissue damage caused by snake bites, so inhibition of their action should interfere with both systemic haemorrhage and local necrosis. Preclinical studies and proteomics studies have shown its effectiveness in many species of snakes and might be particularly attractive given that venom therapy requires only a short duration of treatment (3-5 days), unlike other uses of MMP inhibitors that can produce musculoskeletal toxicity. articles.title: Effectiveness of a pain education programme in cancer pain management: Results from the EFFADOL stepped-wedge trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Pain remains undertreated in 40% of cancer patients with an impact on their quality of life. This study assessed the effectiveness of a Pain Education Programme (PEP) in improving cancer pain management. METHODS: PEP was evaluated through a stepped-wedge pragmatic trial led in 6 independent clusters to compare usual pain care (before staff training) with the educational approach (after training). PEP was delivered in three 2-hour workshops dealing with understanding of pain, managing its treatment, and coping in daily life. The main endpoint was pain interference with daily life. Patients' adherence to PEP, worst pain intensity, anxiety, analgesic adherence, and educational effect of the PEP were evaluated. RESULTS: Among 145 assessable patients, no significant differences were observed in scores of pain interference with daily life between the 2 groups, who experienced substantial improvement. Similarly, worst pain intensity was reduced in both groups, with no added value after the PEP. In the PEP group, intervention significantly improved anxiety (p = 0.009), communication with health professionals (p = 0.028), and patients' knowledge of treatment (98.3% of them vs 88.1%). We found high levels of adherence to the PEP (80%), satisfaction and patients' feelings of having acquired skills in managing their pain after the PEP (>50% of patients rated scores >8.9 on a 0-10 scale). CONCLUSION: No additional benefit of the PEP vs usual care regarding pain interference with daily life was demonstrated. Beyond the fact that patients greatly appreciated the PEP, acquiring skills to better manage their pain and improving communication with health professionals were in line with the goal of therapeutic education. PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: The PEP we applied took into account the French regulatory context concerning the implementation of therapeutic education. This process, although its benefits remain difficult to demonstrate, could enable patients to develop skills to better manage their pain. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03297723, registered on 28, September 2017. (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03297723).

articles.title: Managing trastuzumab deruxtecan-related adverse events in patients with metastatic breast cancer: insights from a worldwide survey of the Hermione EDUcational project.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has shown remarkable efficacy in phase III trials in patients with HER2-positive early- and late-stage breast cancer and HER2-low/ultra-low metastatic breast cancer (mBC). However, toxicities remain prevalent and clinically relevant, leading to dose reductions/interruptions or discontinuation. METHODS: A survey was conducted across oncologists in 13 countries worldwide to collect experiences in managing T-DXd-related toxicities, focusing on nausea/vomiting, fatigue, and interstitial lung disease (ILD) as key areas of clinical concern. RESULTS: Ninety-nine experts participated in the survey. Nausea and fatigue were the most common toxicities, reported by 91.9% and 94.9% of respondents, respectively. 5-HT3 receptor antagonists, NK1 receptor antagonists, and corticosteroids were "very often" prescribed for prophylaxis. The frequency of use of second‑generation 5‑HT3 receptor antagonists varied among respondents. Most frequently, they employed an NK1 receptor antagonist combined with corticosteroids and 5‑HT3 receptor antagonists. Forty-four percent of respondents prescribed 4‑drug regimens incorporating NK1 receptor antagonists and olanzapine to all patients with nausea/vomiting above grade 1 in the first cycle, 35% reserved them for high‑risk patients, and 21% used them for all patients from cycle one. For all respondents, patients receiving T‑DXd experienced fatigue, with 65% observing it in more than 60% of patients, and most considered nausea/vomiting and fatigue to moderately or significantly affect daily activities and quality of life. ILD was reported as rare or occasional and was generally monitored using computed tomography. CONCLUSION: Real-life management of T-DXd-related toxicities is complex and needs an ongoing comprehensive evaluation of patients before, during and after therapy, with a highly trained/skilled multidisciplinary team.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

articles.title: Effects of Ultrasonic Conductance Acupoint Penetration of Dachengqi Decoction on the Recovery of Gastrointestinal Function in Postoperative Patients With Liver Cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal dysfunction is a common complication in patients with liver cancer after surgery, affecting their recovery. The effectiveness of ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration of Dachengqi decoction as a novel treatment method has not been confirmed in patients with liver cancer after surgery. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the effect of ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration into Dachengqi decoction on the recovery of gastrointestinal function in postoperative patients with liver cancer and to provide experience for clinical reference. METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, participants with liver cancer were enrolled from a tertiary hospital in Shandong Province, China. The control group (n = 38) received basic nursing measures, and the intervention group (n = 34) received basic nursing measures combined with ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration of Dachengqi decoction. RESULTS: Compared to the control group, the intervention group demonstrated a significantly shorter postoperative first flatus time, postoperative first defecation time, and time to initiation of food intake. CONCLUSION: The application of ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration of Dachengqi decoction can shorten the first postoperative flatus time, defecation time, and the time of food intake after surgery in postoperative patients with liver cancer. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: In postoperative patients with liver cancer, ultrasonic conductance acupoint penetration of Dachengqi decoction is a secure and straightforward therapeutic approach that can effectively promote the restoration of gastrointestinal function. Future large-scale studies are warranted to replicate the study findings.

articles.title: Secondary Ophthalmic Artery Chemotherapy for Bilateral Retinoblastoma After Incomplete Response to Intravenous Chemotherapy: Initial Prospective Experience from a Resource-Limited Setting.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ophthalmic artery chemotherapy (OAC) is increasingly used for globe salvage in retinoblastoma, but prospective evidence from low- and middle- income countries is scarce. We evaluated short-term outcomes of secondary OAC after insufficient response to intravenous chemotherapy (IVC) with/without focal therapy in a resource- limited setting. MATERIALS & METHODS: In this prospective study (January 2023-June 2025), 21 eyes (5 group B, 5 group C, 8 group D, 3 group E) from 20 children with bilateral retinoblastoma were included; 19 had prior unilateral enucleation. Thirteen eyes underwent bridging OAC after partial IVC response, and eight received rescue OAC for failure or recurrence. Primary endpoints were globe salvage, tumor control, and complications. RESULTS: The cohort included 12 males (60%); median age at diagnosis was 11 months (IQR: 4-18) and at OAC initiation 27 months (IQR: 17-36.5). Eighty-one OAC sessions were delivered (median 4 per eye, IQR: 3-5). After median follow-up of 19 months, overall globe salvage was 76.2% (16/21). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed eye preservation >80% at 12 months and ~70% at 24 months. Complications with permanent sequelae occurred in only one case (5%), with no mortality. Recurrence was observed in 23.5%. Exploratory subgroup analysis showed higher observed globe salvage with among eyes receiving bridging OAC than with among those receiving rescue OAC (100% vs. 37.5%); . However, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because of differences in the two groups differed in baseline disease characteristics, behavior, treatment indication, and underlying chemosensitivity between groups, and the observed association may reflect these factors rather than the timing of OAC alone. Lack of a favorable response after the first OAC cycle was associated with subsequent enucleation (RR = 6.00, 95% CI 1.03-35.91, p=0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This prospective single-center study suggests that secondary OAC is a feasible globe-preserving treatment after incomplete response to IVC with/without focal thrapy in a resource-limited setting. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested higher observed globe salvage with bridging OAC and an association between lack of response after the first OAC session and subsequent enucleation; however, findings should be interpreted cautiously because of small sample size and potential confounding by treatment indication and baseline tumor biology. Larger multicenter studies with longer follow-up are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Lurbinectedin in the therapeutic landscape of SCLC: Key clinical evidence and evolving role in the era of emerging therapies.
articles.abstract: Despite recent therapeutic advances, durable disease control in small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains challenging, particularly after relapse following platinum-based chemo-immunotherapy. Lurbinectedin, a selective inhibitor of oncogenic transcription, has emerged as a novel therapeutic agent with a distinct mechanism of action combining transcription-dependent DNA damage, modulation of the tumor microenvironment, and induction of immunogenic cell death, providing a biological rationale for combination strategies with immunotherapy and other cytotoxic agents. Initially developed as a second-line treatment, lurbinectedin demonstrated clinically meaningful activity in early studies of relapsed SCLC, leading to accelerated regulatory approval. However, subsequent studies have progressively refined its role across different treatment settings. While the phase III ATLANTIS trial did not demonstrate a survival benefit for the combination of lurbinectedin and doxorubicin, emerging data have confirmed its activity and manageable safety profile across heterogeneous patient populations. More recently, the phase III IMforte trial demonstrated improved survival outcomes with maintenance lurbinectedin plus atezolizumab following induction chemo-immunotherapy, expanding its potential role beyond the relapsed setting. Understanding which patients are most likely to benefit from lurbinectedin and how best to integrate this agent into modern treatment strategies represents a key challenge in the management of SCLC. In this review, we summarize the biological rationale, key clinical evidence, and safety profile of lurbinectedin, with particular focus on clinical and molecular predictive factors of response, patient selection and its evolving role within increasingly complex SCLC treatment algorithms.

articles.title: Real-Time Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Monitoring With Digital Triage and Care-Team Integration in Early Breast Cancer: ENABLE Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePROs) can support patient-centered oncology care, but in early breast cancer, it is unclear whether real-time ePRO-triggered triage adds benefit beyond lower-intensity app-based support and scheduled ePRO collection. OBJECTIVE: We tested whether adding weekly ePRO screening, rule-based triage, and care-team escalation to app-based support improves health-related quality of life (HRQoL) during systemic therapy for early breast cancer. METHODS: ENABLE was a multicenter, open-label, parallel-group randomized controlled trial at 2 German university hospitals. Adults with early (stage I-III) breast cancer initiating systemic therapy were randomized 1:1 to reactive patient-reported outcome assessment (RPA) or control. Both arms received the ENABLE app with educational and organizational support and scheduled HRQoL assessments at 6 fixed time points; only RPA received weekly EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale screening (trigger: score <50 or ≥10-point decline) followed by symptom assessment, digital triage, and care-team alerts. Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System-29 was analyzed as an 8-measure HRQoL end-point family (7 domains plus pain intensity); no single domain, composite score, or binary global success rule was prespecified. Group-by-visit mixed-effects models were fitted with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment. The recruitment period was March 22, 2021, to September 8, 2023. RESULTS: Of 605 randomized patients, 487 entered the modified intention-to-treat analysis (RPA: n=242; control: n=245). End-of-treatment between-group differences (RPA minus control, CONCLUSIONS: ENABLE tests real-time, rule-based ePRO triage with care-team escalation against an active digital comparator rather than usual care, isolating the response pathway itself; it extends this design from metastatic disease into early breast cancer and escalates to the care team rather than to the patient alone. Benefits were domain-specific and sub-MID, in anxiety, fatigue, and social participation, tempering the expectation of a global HRQoL effect. For practice, symptom-triggered triage is a supportive-care workflow tool worth embedding where alerts reach a team that acts and documents, not a stand-alone remedy for treatment-related morbidity.

articles.title: Safety and Performance of the Colovac Anastomosis Protection Device. A Pooled Analysis of Prospective Studies Compared With Diverting Loop Ileostomy (SAFE-2025).
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the safety and effectiveness of the Colovac Anastomosis Protection Device with standard diverting ostomy (DO) following low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer. SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: DO is standard of care (SOC) following LAR for rectal cancer but is associated with substantial morbidity. Colovac Device is designed to divert the fecal stream away from the anastomosis intraluminally. METHODS: Three prospective multicenter Colovac trials were pooled and compared with a prospective cohort of patients undergoing LAR with DO for rectal cancer using a propensity score-weighted approach to balance baseline characteristics. The primary safety endpoint for both Colovac and SOC trials was the rate of device-related or stoma-related early major complications by POD10. Secondary endpoints included early anastomotic leak (AL) rates, fecal stream diversion effectiveness, and device migration. RESULTS: Patients were included (Colovac=49, DO=54). By POD10, device- or stoma-related major complications rates were 4.1% (2/49) vs 5.6% (3/54) ( P =0.167). All Colovac devices were successfully placed and retrieved with stoma avoidance achieved in 83.7% at POD10. Major complication rates were similar between groups. Rates of AL detected on POD9/10 were comparable between Colovac and control patients (28.6% vs. 20.4%, P =0.102), with total AL rate of 32.6% in Colovac versus 27.8% ( P =0.342) in control at POD30. Effective fecal diversion was achieved in 91.7% of Colovac patients, with device migration in 14.3%. CONCLUSIONS: Colovac enabled ostomy avoidance in most patients without increasing major complications or AL, suggesting its role as a potential alternative to DO following LAR for rectal cancer. TRIAL REGISTRATION: SAFE-2019: NCT05180565; SAFE-2: NCT05010850; SAFE-2023: NCT06540807; SH-SOC23: NCT06152276.

articles.title: Review of Vaccines for Cancer
articles.abstract: This translational science review examines antigen-based cancer vaccines, which help patients develop immunity to the cellular protein expressed by cancer by stimulating the adaptive immune system.

articles.title: [Corrections] Correction to Lancet Oncol 2025; 26: e423–35
articles.abstract: Concin N, Matias-Guiu X, Cibula D, et al. ESGO–ESTRO–ESP guidelines for the management of patients with endometrial carcinoma: update 2025. Lancet Oncol 2025; 26: e423–35. The appendix of this Policy Review has been corrected as of Oct 26, 2026.

articles.title: [Policy Review] Reporting health-related quality of life in randomised clinical trials evaluating adjuvant systemic therapy: recommendations of Common-Sense Oncology and the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer
articles.abstract: The goal of adjuvant systemic therapy after locoregional treatment of cancer is to increase the probability of cure by eradicating micro-metastases. Adjuvant treatment adds side-effects and can impair health-related quality of life (HRQOL); this must be balanced against a reduction in the probability of recurrence, which has a substantial negative effect on HRQOL. Since many adjuvant therapies lead to small gains in relapse-free or overall survival, the severity and duration of treatment-related side-effects and their impact on patient functioning and overall HRQOL are relevant to clinical decision making.

articles.title: [Policy Review] Development of the Children's Oncology Group long-term follow-up guideline for cancer genetics evaluation in childhood cancer survivors
articles.abstract: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing.

articles.title: [Policy Review] Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations
articles.abstract: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67–79% agreement).

articles.title: Toward the next generation of CAR T cell therapies for cancer
articles.abstract: CAR T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of blood cancers but faces persistent challenges in solid tumors. In this review, Usta and Mackall synthesize clinical lessons, next-generation engineering strategies, and emerging in vivo manufacturing approaches to define opportunities for broader, safer, and more effective CAR T cell therapies.

articles.title: AI for detection of adverse events in the real world
articles.abstract:
Nature Cancer, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01258-4

Immune-related adverse events are common in cancer immunotherapy and can be difficult to recognize in clinical routine. Work now shows that an agentic AI system built around a large language model can identify such events in prospectively collected clinical notes and can make human review of such notes faster and more consistent.
